01-blog-sourdough.why: X has a more personal voice but adds 'finally stopped worrying', while Y stays closer to the original claims.
Y has a stronger personal voice but invents details like forgetting to feed the starter and having stopped worrying, while X stays close to the original.

02-blog-remote-work.why: Y sounds like a real lead writing, but it invents 'that one still bothers me', which X avoids.
X sounds more personal but adds an invented feeling ('that one still bothers me'), while Y adds nothing.

03-blog-product-launch.why: X drops the announcement boilerplate but invents invoices that 'send themselves on a schedule'.
Y is plainer and drops the announcement boilerplate, but X keeps the 'invoicing tool for freelancers' framing more exactly and Y's 'send themselves on a schedule' is a small addition.

04-email-deadline.why: Both keep every fact, and Y's tone is warmer and less curt than X's 'tell me what time does'.
Both keep every fact; X's thanks for flexibility sounds more like a real colleague than Y's blunter wording.

05-email-followup.why: Y is tighter and more natural, and both keep all the required facts.
Both keep all the facts; X is tighter, while Y's closing 'keep talking about where we could help' still has some sales filler.

06-email-decline.why: Y flows more naturally as a decline note, and both preserve the facts.
The two are nearly identical and keep every fact; X cuts the formulaic 'I'm honored' line.

07-tech-readme.why: X adds a 'skips repeated work' benefit line, while Y keeps the 'future release' wording plain and true to the original.
Y adds an unsupported benefit claim ('skips repeated work'); otherwise the two are equivalent.

08-tech-postmortem.why: X drops the aphorism, but its lessons section says the outage 'took down checkout', which overstates the 30% failure rate.
Y swaps the stock aphorism for a concrete lesson but overstates the impact by saying the outage 'took down checkout' when only 30% of requests failed.

09-tech-pr-description.why: X adds an invented rationale about how the vendor delivers events, and Y omits the fluffy Why section.
Y adds an invented rationale section ('fits how the vendor delivers events') that the original does not support.

10-essay-cities.why: Y reads more naturally, but X keeps the essay's explicit argument for removing parking minimums.
Y ends on a clear position where X's last line is limp; both keep every fact, with small rewordings of the original's claims.

11-essay-reading.why: Y cuts the cliche opener and closer, while X keeps more of the original's claims.
X drops the cliched 'window into worlds' opening and the moralizing close, but Y keeps more of the original's claims.

12-essay-ai-art.why: Y has a real first-person voice but reinterprets the consent problem, which X states as the original does.
Y keeps a grand closing line about unrealized potential, while X's conclusion is concrete; both keep all four facts.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: Y names the test and ties the cause to the intermittent failures in a natural reply, and it keeps every fact.
Both are faithful; X names the test and ties the cause to the intermittent failures, which reads like a real thread reply.

14-slack-meeting.why: Y reads as a smoother single DM, and both keep all three facts.
Both keep all three facts; X flows as one natural DM, while Y's first two sentences are slightly choppy.

15-slack-review.why: X engages Ken conversationally and ends on a check-in, and both keep the technical facts.
Y addresses Ken and checks back with him the way a real review reply would; both keep every fact.

16-academic-abstract.why: X hedges to fit the correlational design, while Y keeps the causal overclaim that improving sleep would help.
Y notes the correlational design and drops the causal overclaim, while X still claims that improving sleep could help students perform better.

17-academic-discussion.why: X hedges the generalization and reliability claims to fit the evidence, while Y keeps 'probably reflect' and 'reliable'.
Y hedges the generalizability and reliability claims to match the evidence, while X keeps the 'probably reflect broader trends' overclaim.

18-academic-litreview.why: The two are nearly identical, and Y drops the puffy 'seminal' while both keep all the facts.
Both keep all the facts and citations; Y keeps the puffery word 'seminal'.
